t: None of the funds made available by this Act may be used to provide arms, training, or other assistance to the Azov Battalion.

fable.w: This is a funding restriction that bars the use of appropriated funds for assistance to a particular entity. The only tempting reading is that it mentions an outside group, but the Azov Battalion is the object of the prohibition, not a party consulted in any federal decision. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, rulemaking, or right to sue.
fable.s: None of the funds made available by this Act may be used to provide arms, training, or other assistance to the Azov Battalion.

qwen_block.w: This section is a funding restriction that prohibits the federal government from providing assistance to a specific group. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process with parties outside the federal government. There is no advisory board, public comment period, or requirement to consult with states, tribes, or the public.
qwen_block.s: None of the funds made available by this Act may be used to provide arms, training, or other assistance to the Azov Battalion.

opus.w: This provision only says that funds in the Act cannot be used to give arms, training, or other assistance to the Azov Battalion. It sets up no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue. Mentioning an outside group as a possible recipient of aid is different from letting outside parties help shape a federal decision.
opus.b: 1. **Reasoning:** One might read "assistance to the Azov Battalion" as the government dealing with an outside party. That reading fails. The provision only bars the use of funds. No one outside the federal government is consulted, sits on an advisory body, comments, takes part in a hearing, or gets a right to sue before a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a substantive restriction on the use of federal funds. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or input from parties outside the federal government (such as states, tribes, the public, or experts) before a decision is made. It simply prohibits a specific action.
qwen_chat.s: None of the funds made available by this Act may be used to provide arms, training, or other assistance to the Azov Battalion.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the restriction implies a decision-making process involving outside parties (e.g., Congress debating the restriction), but the text itself is a substantive prohibition on spending, not a procedural requirement for participation. It does not mandate consultation, hearings, or input from any outside entity.
